catalog_quote: Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length) Stress is penultimate and shifts with the addition of another syllable to remain so: baba'bao 'uncles'. In some 3 syllable words stress shifts to antipenultimate, but even this fluctuates with individual speakers. Words longer than 2 or 3 syllables fall into patterns of 2 or 3 syllables with secondary stress but retain the main penultimate stress: yabayaba'bana 'ugly'. Stressed syllables tend to be lengthened.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress falls on the penultimate syllable of the word and moves rightward when a syllable (suffix) is added so that it stays penultimate. Some trisyllabic words are stressed on the antepenult instead, with speaker-to-speaker fluctuation. Stressed syllables tend to be lengthened; no contrastive tone or length is reported.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Longer words are grouped into 2- or 3-syllable units each carrying secondary stress, with main stress remaining penultimate (example yabayaba'bana 'ugly'); direction/alternation not stated more precisely.
new_statements.exceptions: In some three-syllable words stress falls on the antepenultimate, and this fluctuates between individual speakers. CVC syllables arise from loss of a final vowel in some CVmV sequences (yam, lem.hi), but no weight effect on stress is claimed.
new_statements.identity_note: The OPD describes Auhelawa [KUD] of Milne Bay Province (Dobu-Duau network) as worked on by SIL from 1983 (Lithgow); no sub-dialect is singled out.
